unit_reason: Each probe label is one relationship to one anchor. Five people also have a replay, which is a second row and not a second resolution. Cluster scores are not computed.

examples.title: Correct automatic association
examples.notes: Same person. The probe has no email, so the name is the singular identifier, and the birthday matches.

examples.title: Correct separation
examples.notes: Different person. Different first name and a birthday one year later, so no block key hits. Never scored.

examples.title: Incorrect automatic association
examples.notes: Distinct family member, shared email, probe birthday missing. A missing birthday keeps the email hard match.

examples.title: Incorrect automatic association marked indistinguishable
examples.notes: Distinct namesake, same name and birthday, probe has no email. Exact name plus the same birthday is a hard match. The fields on the probe do not separate the two people.

examples.title: Missed duplicate
examples.notes: Same person, new email, probe birthday missing. The email misses and there is no birthday to block on, so the row is new.

examples.title: Same person held for review
examples.notes: Same person, nickname, different email and ZIP, same birthday. The name and birthday keep a low score in review.

examples.title: Different people held for review
examples.notes: Distinct family member, shared email, both birthdays present and different. The email birthday review opens. The original person keeps the email.

examples.title: Replay of an earlier row
examples.notes: Byte-identical copy of the anchor. The import row key matches, so the resolver is not called and the stored path stays the anchor path B.

examples.title: Import error for a different person
examples.notes: Distinct person, same phone, nothing else shared. The matcher does not read the phone, so the row is new. The second phone write then fails.

examples.title: Import error for the same person
examples.notes: Same person, same phone, new email, different ZIP, same name and birthday. The 0.60 threshold keeps a name-and-birthday agreement in review, and the different ZIP keeps the score below 0.85, so the path stays D. The second phone write then fails.

examples.title: First MB-3 probe
examples.notes: Distinct namesake. The anchor has an email and no birthday. The probe has the same name, no email, and a birthday. A missing stored birthday keeps the name hard match.

examples.title: First MB-4 probe
examples.notes: Same person. The anchor has an email and no birthday. The probe has the same name, no email, and a birthday. A missing stored birthday keeps the name hard match.
